en: The Mañjuśrī-bodhisattva-mūla-mahātantra-rāja-sūtra,
Chapter on the Golden-Winged Garuda King, in one fascicle.
Compiled by the Grand Master of the Imperial Household, Peer of the State, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Sui.

The Imperially Enfeoffed Lord of Three Thousand Households, conferred the purple robe and the title of Minister of Works, posthumously honored with the epithet "Great Mirror" (Dajian), bearing the title of Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, translated by imperial decree. At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha...
He further observed the palaces of the Śuddhāvāsa devas and addressed the youthful Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, saying:
"Mañjuśrī, within your Great Teaching..."
It is praised and rejoiced in by all Tathāgatas;
it accords with the practice of Mahāmantra,
for the purpose of causing all sentient beings to enter the samaya-maṇḍala.
By mastering the five elements— earth, water, fire, wind, and space— and through this knowledge,
one penetrates the inconceivable realm of the speech of all sentient beings and achieves the mantra practice of the King of the Garuḍas.
Through supernatural powers, one awakens to this and masters skillful means;
thus all mundane and supramundane dharmas are fully accomplished,
even extending to the bodily dharmas of all animals and the kings of the garuḍas, which are all thoroughly penetrated.
Therefore, in the midst of the great assembly of bodhisattvas,
the King of the Garuḍas, surrounded by immeasurable garuḍas,
rose from his seat and approached the presence of the Great Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.
Prostrating with his head at [Mañjuśrī’s] feet, he knelt with palms joined and addressed Mañjuśrī, saying,
“I abide in the stage of a great bodhisattva.”
In order to bring benefit, welfare, and happiness to all sentient beings through this king of teachings,
one hundred kinds of dharmas of the past have been taught;
we pray that the Great Bodhisattva will graciously consent to explain them with sympathetic joy.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva said,
"Speak now for the benefit of sentient beings. Then,
through the Buddha's majestic spiritual power, the King of the Garuḍas [spoke].
Rising from his seat, he leaped for joy.
Mañjuśrī said, "You should proclaim the hundred kinds of dharmas of the past, along with their profound and secret essential teachings."
At that time, the King of the Garuḍas spoke this mantra:

*Namo samantabuddhānām | apratihata-sāsane | tadyathā | oṃ śakuna mahāśakuna vidanta pākṣa sarvabandha-gaṇaka kha kha khahi khahi samaya manu-samara hūṃ tiṣṭha modita-stava kiñcabāyati svāhā.* Then, the King of the Garuḍas, having spoken the mantra, [remained silent].
Next, I shall proclaim one hundred past dharmas concerning the summoning,
taming, and seizing of nāgas—
both those who have been bitten by nāgas and those who have not.
It causes spirits to manifest and recount all matters of the past and future;
it summons serpents to punish them, extracts venom from serpents for theatrical display,
and ensures one is not harmed by poison while summoning all manner of poisons.
Either one merely recites the name with mental intention,
or one performs the rite mentally;
the practitioner who maintains the recitation shall observe the fast for three days and abstain from food.
Or, having fasted for twelve days,
one should construct a six-cubit maṇḍala using five-colored powders on the bank of a river.
Paint eight eight-petaled lotus flowers.
In the center, paint the Buddha in the posture of preaching the Dharma.
To the right of the Buddha, draw the Great Holy Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī using colored powder.
One should form the añjali mudrā and gaze up at the features of the Buddha.
To the left of the Buddha, one should depict the deity Nārāyaṇa,
who has four arms holding four types of insignia and weapons.
Near Nārāyaṇa, one should paint the King of Birds with golden plumage,
depicted in an extremely terrifying and fearsome form.
Near the King of the Garuḍas,
paint the deity Āloṇa behind the Great Sage Mañjuśrī.
Paint the Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa, the youth Sudhana,
and Subhūti standing with palms joined.
This is called the middle mandala.
Next, on the outer court to the east of the maṇḍala, draw a vajra using white lime;
on the left side, draw a sword using charcoal powder.
On the northern side, draw a yellow staff;
on the western side, draw a red noose.
In this manner, arrange the maṇḍala within the outer enclosure.
Once the painting is finished,
one should offer three kinds of sweet foods to its four sides.
Upon the altar, one should scatter various flowers, as well as various types of ointments and powdered incense.
Furthermore, place an arghya vessel and a kumbha jar filled with scented water;
burn agalloch incense and recite the root mantra to invite all the holy assemblies.
In front of this mandala, one should construct a homa fire pit.
Light it with smokeless charcoal and cast pieces of khadira wood into it.
Then, arouse a mind of great compassion toward all sentient beings.

Assume the posture of a nāga seat and sit with knees pressed together. Using wood from a snake-stung tree, mix three sweets—curd, honey, and clarified butter—and cast them into the fire one thousand and eight times.
Upon the signs of accomplishment appearing, a multitude of snakes will immediately gather there.
One should immediately offer arghya.
Know that the mantra practice has been accomplished;
one should recite the mantra while making this aspiration:
"May the mantra-dharma attain siddhi.
Then, reciting the root mantra, he dispatches [the deity].
He follows the recitation of the mantra with argha water.
Sprinkle all the offered food, drink, flowers,
and incense into the river water;
from this point onward, perform the following.
The hook-summoning [mantra] prohibits all types of poisons;
success is achieved by reciting it accordingly.
Furthermore, there is a method for causing two people to hate one another.
Take white cotton flowers mixed with poison and perform *homā* twenty-one times; they will then become mutually hostile.
Furthermore, there is a method for destroying an enemy.
Take a single snake skin and recite the mantra once;
by casting it into the fire twenty-one times, that enemy will be crushed and destroyed.
Furthermore, there is another method: take bird wings and perform *homa* twenty-one times.
That enemy will run about wildly like a jumping crow.
Furthermore, regarding the method for causing men and women to love one another:
by performing *homa* twenty-one times with white mustard seeds mixed with clarified butter (*sarpis*), they will immediately become respectful and harmonious toward each other.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause a king to feel respect and affection,
one should perform *homa* with milk porridge twenty-one times, and one will immediately obtain whatever one desires.
Another method is that by consecrating a clod of earth and casting it into the fire, the fire will not grow hot.
If one wishes to release the consecration, simply casting the grass into the fire will undo it.
Furthermore, there is another method: by reciting the mantra seven times to consecrate a river, stream, or spring, no fish therein shall be caught in nets.
Furthermore, there is a method: by snapping one's fingers while reciting the mantra, one can summon all the fish.
Moreover, there is a method for those who suffer from any illness.
Consecrate water twenty-one times and pour it upon the crown of the head; the illness will be cured immediately.
Furthermore, there is another method: consecrate a staff twenty-one times.
When one strikes all the gates, the gates open of their own accord.
Furthermore, there is another method: place a staff inside a blue-colored bag and display it from afar before the enemy lines on the battlefield.
That army will immediately disperse.
Furthermore, there is a method: empower the lapels of one's garment twenty-one times;
this will cause one to dazzle and confound the enemy.
All the swords, staves, bows, and crossbows belonging to that army will spontaneously shatter and be rendered immobile.
If one wishes to release them, reciting the mantra once will cause them to be released immediately.
Furthermore, there is a method: take the head of a snake, empower ashes with mantras, and block its mouth.
While reciting the mantra twenty-one times and calling out the person's name, that person will immediately become mute.
Furthermore, there is a method for one who has been struck by a poisoned arrow.
If one sprinkles consecrated water from afar upon the arrow, it will immediately come forth.
Furthermore, if one desires to neutralize another’s mantra,
by reciting this mantra, that [mantra] shall become ineffective.
If one wishes for immediate liberation, there is another method:
empower twenty-one bricks with mantras and cast them at those who are bound in shackles and fetters. They will be released.
Immediately the shackles and manacles shall be broken.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause rain to fall,
one should establish and perform offerings according to the previously described altar ritual.
Furthermore, when constructing a homa hearth, take *kaṭhilla* wood and kindle a fire.
Perform one thousand and eight oblations (*homa*) with white mustard seeds, and a sweet rain will immediately fall.
If more rain is required, perform the homa again.
Even up to a thousand billion [beings], all shall obtain their desires as they wish.
Furthermore, there is a method: take *pippalī* (long pepper) and empower it twenty-one times;
holding it in the hand, wherever one waves it in any direction, [the result follows].
All evil frost and hail will immediately shift elsewhere.
Furthermore, if a house or dwelling is being consumed by fire,
by performing the aforementioned rite, the fire disaster will immediately shift to other locations.
Furthermore, if there is rain or snow, one should perform this same rite;
know that it is to be conducted according to the previous method.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one empowers a clay snake twenty-one times.
Having spoken these words, "Bite so-and-so," one then bites that person according to the assigned location.
Furthermore, there is another method: one may fashion a snake using charcoal powder, following the same procedure as before.
If one wishes to release them, recite the mantra saying "release," and they will immediately be released.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one wishes to summon a snake.
Consecrate white mustard seeds seven times and cast them in the four directions;
the snakes will immediately come to respond to the boundary-binding.
Sprinkle water upon them, and they will be dispatched.
Furthermore, there is a method: empower a clod of earth twenty-one times and throw it into a dragon pool, and the dragon will immediately come forth.
Another method: empower earth and throw it into water.
The nāga immediately surges forth;
the practitioner stands upon the nāga’s back and attains mastery over all.
Furthermore, there is another method: if one is bitten by a snake and poisoned, [the following should be done].
Fashion four garuḍas out of clay;
recite the mantra and sprinkle water upon their bodies,
then cast the garuḍas in the four directions.
Each of them then brought a snake, holding it in its mouth;
the practitioner said this:
"Drink that man's poison."
It will immediately dissolve, and one will then be able to stand up.
Furthermore, there is another method: empower small beans one hundred and eight times and scatter them in the four directions;
the nāgas will then arrive and transform themselves into the shape of bees.
If one says, "Sting such-and-such a person," that bee will immediately sting them;
no practitioner of recitation can undo this.
The practitioner of the rite sprinkles consecrated water upon it, and its poison is immediately neutralized and dissipated.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a bow and, having consecrated an arrow, shoot it in the four directions.
Then a snake, wrapped around an arrow, returns;
the practitioner speaks these words:
"Drink this poison."
The person who was bitten immediately stands up;
one should know that this applies when the arrow does not have an iron tip.
Furthermore, there is another method: if anyone is struck by a poisoned arrow, [one should perform the following].
When one empowers a water-arrow, that arrow will immediately emerge.
Furthermore, there is another method: fashion four weasels out of ant-mound clay;
empower them with water and sprinkle it upon their bodies.
The mongoose immediately went away and returned carrying the snake in its mouth.
The practitioner said, "Drink this poison," and the poison was instantly neutralized;
the person who had been bitten stood up at once.
Furthermore, there is a method for consecrating charcoal:
draw a snake upon the ground and lash it with a staff made of *argha* wood.
The painted snake immediately went off to fetch a real snake, which it brought back and bit.
The person who had been bitten and died then rose up and drank the venom itself. Once the poison was consumed, the deceased person immediately revived.
Furthermore, by empowering a banner and parasol with this rite,
those who have died from poisoning will be revived as soon as they are brushed with them.
Furthermore, by empowering musical instruments with this rite and then playing, striking, or blowing them, [the same result is achieved].
All those who have died from poisoning shall immediately revive.
Furthermore, if one wishes to summon dragons or snakes,
one should dye soil with five colors and draw a maṇḍala.
Clapping one's hands, recite the mantra;
immediately, dragons and snakes will come from the four directions and enter the mandala.
One should not feel fear.
By binding the topknot as a protection for the body, one will not dare to cause harm.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one uses this mantra to empower the eyes; by looking at a person who is angry or wrathful [with these empowered eyes], [they will be subdued].
In an instant he fell to the ground;
he immediately transformed into a snake.
If one wished for him to be released, he would be released.
Furthermore, by reciting the mantra in this manner,
those who have been poisoned as well as those who are not susceptible to poison will all experience divine efficacy and attain mastery.
Furthermore, there is another method: take withered flowers that have been offered to Nārāyaṇa,
recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times to empower them,
and then cast them onto a crossroads or into a person's house.
When the flower transforms into a snake, it is able to bite people.
If one consecrates water with mantras and sprinkles it upon them,
the poison of those who have been bitten will be immediately neutralized.
Furthermore, there is a method for consecrating one's own hands;
by practicing this for six months, one will not be harmed by any poisons.
Furthermore, there is a method for consecrating one's own body while speaking these words:
If a snake bites that person, it will immediately bite [the practitioner].
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one consecrates a crown, necklaces, and various ornaments with dhāraṇī-mantras;
by wearing these upon the body, one can protect oneself.
One will not be afflicted by any poisons.
Furthermore, if someone has been poisoned to the point of death,
one should recite the mantra near that person's side.
Whether by smearing with mud, sprinkling with water,
fanning with a fan, or mentally reciting the mantra,
those who have died from poison shall immediately revive.
Furthermore, according to another method, if someone is emaciated,
one should empower *mahā-maṅgalya* mixed with clarified butter;
by burning it as incense for that person, they will immediately become robust, full, and well-nourished.
Furthermore, there is another method: grind human bone into powder,
and while burning it, recite the mantra for the owl and the screech-owl.
If one adds that person's name within the mantra, that person will perish.
Furthermore, regarding the method for reciting the mantra:
empower *maṇḍana* medicine and use it among the aforementioned medicines; likewise, burn husks of grain.
This will cause that person to become insane.
Furthermore, there is a method: mix white mustard seeds with [other ingredients], burn them while reciting the mantra and adding the person's name.
One will then be afflicted by a malarial fever that is difficult to cure.
Furthermore, there is a method: take *yiyiren* (coix lacryma-jobi) mixed with cat dung;
burn it while reciting the mantra to empower it.
This causes those people to harbor mutual hatred.
Furthermore, there is a method using powdered skulls, powdered dried frogs, powdered dried fish, and honey.
By reciting mantras while burning [the substances], one empowers them to sever the life-force of that person.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one burns ox gall and human bone mixed with clarified butter to destroy enemies.
Furthermore, there is another method: take fish roe, liquor, *karpāsa* (cotton) flowers, and *madhyaka* seeds;
mix them together and empower them by reciting the mantra.
If a person is separated from others and dwelling at a distance, [this shall bring them back].
If one recites that person's name, they will return before long.
Furthermore, there is another method: grind *kṛṣṇa-tila* (black sesame) beans into a powder, and [combine it] with chicken meat and chicken eggs.
Grind them together and form them into pills the size of jujube fruits;
by burning them while reciting the name of the target, one will achieve summoning.
Furthermore, there is another method: grind radish seeds.
Burn it with sesame oil;
this is the method for the swift incense of summoning (*ākarṣaṇa*).
Furthermore, there is another method: mix *agaru* (sandalwood) incense with clarified butter (*ghṛta*).
By burning [the substances] while reciting the name of that person, one cures all diseases.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs *homa* with sesame seeds mixed with white mustard for seven nights.
By uttering that person's name, one immediately gains their respect, affection, and submission.
Furthermore, there is another method: mix salt and mustard seeds together and perform *homa* one thousand and eighty times.
By performing this three times daily for seven days, one will gain the respect and affection of great beings.
Furthermore, there is another method: take a skull, grind it finely into powder, and empower it one hundred and eighty times with mantras.
By smearing it on one's hands and touching others, one immediately gains their respect and affection.
Furthermore, there is another method: take ash from a śītavana (charnel ground) and empower it one hundred and eight times.
If one scatters [the powder] upon that person's body, they will immediately suffer from severe malaria.
Later, if they resolve their mind to repent,
they will be released from it through the empowerment of this mantra.
Furthermore, there is another method: take the fur of a mongoose, white mustard seeds, and snake skin, mix them together to form a powder.
Recite the mantra one hundred and eight times over the name of the person concerned, then burn it.
If one wishes to reverse the situation so that all people who currently hate that person instead come to hold them in affection and obtain wealth and treasures,
one should perform a homa by burning consecrated sesame seeds.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one blends sesame seeds, non-glutinous rice, and clarified butter,
burns them while reciting the mantra with empowerment;
by this, one gains the respect and love of women.
Furthermore, there is another method: using barley, sesame, and the fat and marrow of a frog, perform *homa* for three nights beside a dragon pond.
Heaven will then send down heavy rain.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one fashions the form of a garuḍa out of clay and places it within one's own hands joined in the gesture of homage (añjali).
One should then enter the water until it reaches the chest.
At the hour of midnight, call out the person's name and recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times; thus, subjugation will be accomplished.
Furthermore, there is another method: scatter non-glutinous rice in a cemetery and then gather it back up.
Each time one takes a grain and recites the mantra once,
striking it against the heart of the Garuḍa,
one will immediately obtain official rank and emolument, as well as all one's kinsmen and retinue.
Furthermore, there is a method: by burning the fur of a mongoose, mouse hair, and the seeds within cotton flowers together while reciting the mantra,
all ghosts and spirits will be filled with reverence and affection.
One can direct them as one pleases, and they will all accomplish whatever is required.
Furthermore, there is a method: by mixing *viṣapāla* with honey and burning it, one will achieve the state of being held in loving-kindness.
Furthermore, there is a method: using the powder of a red chicken’s skull mixed with red mustard-seed oil and burned, one immediately achieves the rite of subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*).
Another method involves using *pāṭala* flowers, *tagara*, and *mānaka* medicinal flowers.
When burned together, it immediately brings about attraction.
Furthermore, there is another method: by burning fennel seeds, devadāru wood, frog excrement, and so forth together, one immediately achieves attraction.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one mixes barley, sesame, *māluka* grass, and *elā* with cow urine and burns them;
this immediately brings about subjugation (*vaśīkaraṇa*).
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one uses realgar, *kākajaṅghā*, and one’s own *rudhira*.
If one burns [incense] while reciting the person's name, that person will immediately become mute.
Furthermore, there is a method: by burning human hair, beef, and sesame seeds together with oil, one causes another to fall ill.
Furthermore, there is a method: using the feathers of a crow and an owl mixed with bitter oil (kṣāra-taila), burn them while reciting the name of the evil person;
this will immediately effect their expulsion.
If he does not become compliant, he shall depart immediately.
Furthermore, there is a method: mix *agaru* incense, clarified butter, and the juice of the three fruits.
Perform the fire offering (homa) while reciting the mantra; all people will then revere and love you.
Furthermore, there is another method: use zero-ling-xiang (nāgakeśara), Indian cinnamon, and su-he-xiang (stacte).
By performing the recitation while burning these three substances together,
one causes all people to become compliant and to respectfully follow one's instructions.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein ghee is combined with white sandalwood, camphor, and the *añjana* medicinal herb.
By burning [incense], the recitation is honored and the noble ones rejoice.
Furthermore, there is another method: one should sit upon a mahāmāṣa before an image of Nārāyaṇa.
First, perform eight rounds of *homa* offerings.
Then, recite the mantra one thousand and eight times.
By performing this rite for three nights, all that is sought shall be attained.
Furthermore, there is another method: in a charnel ground,
one should fashion the form of that person using the ashes from the charnel ground and burn the flesh of a large beast as incense.
Sitting upon a mat of straw, recite this one thousand times;
whatever you seek shall be obtained, those who are sought shall all come,
and all that you command shall be carried out.
Furthermore, there is a method: by performing a *homa* sacrifice with cotton flowers mixed with chaff and a crow’s wing for a single *kṣaṇa*, one causes that person to be driven away.
Another method is to kindle a fire with *udumbara* wood in a cemetery.
One should use *karpāsa* (cotton) as a seat.
By burning snake skins, the food in one's household shall never be exhausted.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one grinds bones from a charnel ground into powder.
Perform one thousand and eight *homa* offerings with white mustard seeds while reciting the name of the person;
all within a radius of one hundred *yojanas* will be summoned.
This [protects] against the faults of attachment to various forms, desires, and tactile sensations.
Furthermore, there is a method: using white sandalwood,
carve the form of the King of the Golden-Winged Birds (Garuda) with outspread wings,
adorned with all the necklaces and ornaments of the nāgas.
Its beak and claws are made extremely sharp and keen;
it assumes a terrifying and fearsome form,
standing upon a lotus pedestal.
One should adopt the posture of looking downward;
this may be done with a separate piece of wood or by drawing it upon a wall.
The artisan must observe the eight precepts (*aṣṭāṅga-śīla*).
One should double the price paid to ensure they are made joyful;
it should be about the size of one span.
Before this image, perform all activities;
whatever one seeks shall be accomplished without exception.
Furthermore, for those who wish to seek increase (*puṣṭi*):
Fashion an image of the King of the Garuḍas from vibhītaka wood;
by reciting before it, all that one seeks shall be attained.
Furthermore, there is a method for those who wish to seek the object of their affection.
If one fashions an image from udumbara wood and performs recitation before it,
one will immediately achieve the power of attraction (*vaśīkaraṇa*).
Furthermore, there is another method for those who seek children or a herd of cattle.
One may fashion an image from *nyagrodha* wood.
Furthermore, for one who wishes to seek wealth,
one should fashion an image from *mṛdvīkā* wood.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs homa with pork;
the fruit of this practice will be accomplished.
Moreover, there is a method for those who seek official rank.
Perform homa with horse meat.
Furthermore, according to another method, perform homa with the flesh of the black śāla bird to seek auspicious blessings.
Furthermore, according to the ritual method for seeking fame and renown that spreads everywhere,
as well as for seeking women or land,
one should perform homa by burning the flesh of large beasts.
Furthermore, when seeking to prevail in logical debate,
one should likewise perform the homa of tiger meat and *maṃsa*;
success will then be achieved.
Furthermore, there is a method for seeking victory in battle:
by performing a homa with the flesh of a large predator,
one will certainly achieve victory.
Furthermore, there is a method for seeking the respect and affection of powerful kings:
by performing *homa* with elephant meat, one will achieve their submission and devotion.
Additionally, there is a method for dealing with those who are arrogant due to royal favor, those who possess great power, and high-ranking ministers.
By performing *homa* with *aśvagandhā*— here called *brāhmaṇasparśā*— one will gain their reverence and submission.
Furthermore, according to another rite, one may cause them to lose their lives by performing *homa* while burning elephant hair and reciting their names.
Furthermore, there is a method: carve an image of a garuḍa from jomana wood;
by reciting mantras before this image, the life of that [enemy] shall be severed.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs recitation before a golden image to accomplish the rite of augmentation (*puṣṭi*).
There is also a method wherein one performs recitation before a silver image.
One seeks renown that is heard everywhere.
Furthermore, there is a method: by performing *homa* with the feathers of a crow, one is able to cause harm to the opponent.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs homa with vulture feathers to effect killing.
Additionally, there is a method wherein one performs homa with the wings of an owl.
It can cause mutual enmity.
Furthermore, by performing homa with peacock feathers,
one obtains wealth and treasures.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs homa with the feathers of a wild cock;
this results in an abundance of wives and concubines.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs homa with the wings of a sparrow.
One will have many children.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one seeks gold,
one should burn bird feathers.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs homa with the wing of an owl;
this can cause the target to fall into a state of stupor.
Furthermore, there is a method wherein one performs homa with dog meat.
One can cause others to lose their lives.
Furthermore, there is a method for performing homa with beef to accomplish summoning.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause harm to another,
one should perform homa with the flesh of a large predatory beast. Furthermore, if one wishes to pacify calamities, [one should perform homa with other substances].
Perform homa with deer hair.
Furthermore, if one wishes to destroy a city,
perform homa by burning the wool of a black sheep.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause mutual hatred between people,
one should perform homa with human hair. Moreover,
if one wishes to cause harm to another, [one should perform homa with human hair].
One may also perform homa with human hair,
which is further capable of destroying enemies;
such rites as these involve performing homa for seven days during the three periods of the day.
If one merely recollects me,
all poisons can be eliminated;
if one constantly recites my name, one can accomplish all tasks.
Blessed One, if anyone practices this mantra from this Great King of Teachings by reciting it at the three times of day,
I shall always eliminate all calamities and misfortunes for them.
One should always follow behind that person.
At that time, the King of the Garuḍas taught his own hand-seal:
one should interlace the two thumbs.
The two hands are held in the manner of folded wings;
by forming this mudrā, one accomplishes the Body Mudrā.
This was previously taught by Mahāmaheśvara.
If all the nāgas see this seal,
they will all be completely dissolved and will not dare to disobey the command.
This is done by lowering the remaining fingers and beckoning them back and forth.
The mantra for the seal of summoning the nāgas is as follows:
Oṃ jyāḥ. This seal and mantra can subdue the nāgas, and can also subdue those who are difficult to subdue.
Furthermore, join the two hands in *añjali* like an unopened lotus flower;
insert both thumbs inside and clench each hand into a fist, then join them together.
This mudrā is named the "Subduer of All Dragons in Heaven and Among Men" and can accomplish all things. Furthermore,
it is said that for this mudrā, one joins the two hands in *añjali*.
The two ring fingers are crossed outwardly behind the middle fingers;
the two thumbs are placed side by side and slightly bent like a mouth;
and the two index fingers each hook the ring finger.
Join the two little fingers together and extend them upright.
Using the root mantra, this is called the Vidyujjvāla-mukha-mahāgaruḍendra-mudrā (the Seal of the Great King of Garuḍas with Radiant Light).
It is also called the Seal for Terrifying All Nāgas.
This is the method of practice among all the mantras I have taught,
according to the rules set forth in the worldly Garuḍa Sūtra.
In all cases, one employs this mantra and mudrā to accomplish auxiliary activities out of compassion for all sentient beings.
This King of Fundamental Teachings has been proclaimed;
one should always seek accomplishment within this supreme teaching,
which brings about most excellent benefit for all sentient beings.
In the future, during the age of the final dharma,
one shall use this to protect and uphold the Buddha-dharma,
and to defend kings and their realms.
May all sentient beings attain peace and happiness.
This dharma-gate must be carefully selected for those who are vessels of the Dharma and who possess pure faith in the Triple Gem.
Abiding in the bodhicitta and feeling deep compassion for sentient beings,
one should be filial and obedient toward one's parents, loyal and respectful toward the king,
and honor one's preceptors and ācāryas.
Those who possess all faculties complete and have deep faith in the mantra dharma,
being free from doubt regarding attainment in this very life,
shall give rise to profound yearning and diligently seek this teaching.
Regarding those who do not begrudge their own bodies or lives:
if the ācārya sees such persons earnestly making their request,
he shall cause them to prepare the requisites for the maṇḍala.
Then, one should establish the maṇḍala as previously described.
One should cause the disciples to be pure through fasting and observance of precepts,
and confer upon them the three refuges and the bodhicitta vow.
He is led into the maṇḍala.
He casts a flower toward the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Nārāyaṇa, the Garuḍa Kings, and the various devas.
Such a person is fit to be a vessel for the Dharma.
One should be entitled to hear [the Dharma] and worthy to receive this teaching; yet,
if the flower cast does not land upon the assembly of noble ones, [one is not so entitled].
In this dharma, there is also no section on accomplishment.
Once one has attained [the state of] attachment,
then before this maṇḍala, with the root mantra:
Consecrate the scented water three times and make this vow:
"After receiving this dharma..."
One must never speak of this to those who have not yet entered the maṇḍala.
One should not treat the ācārya with contempt or betray his kindness.
If one can maintain this vow throughout this life, [one shall attain success].
Siddhi will manifest before you,
and in a future life, you shall be born within the palace of the Great Sage Mañjuśrī. However,
if you divulge [the teachings] or betray his kindness, [you shall suffer].
Consequently, one will surely meet with premature death, encounter many calamities and disasters,
and fall into the evil realms in the future.
Having thus made this vow, [he continued:]
Have them drink the water of the oath.
Following the ācārya, they shall one by one undergo discernment regarding the upholding, receiving, and recitation [of the teachings].
They must not commit acts of harm on account of minor transgressions or faults.
In whatever Dharma practice one performs,
if one generates such a mind as to benefit many people, to protect and defend the boundaries of the nation, and to uphold the Buddha-Dharma;
With little exertion of effort, one swiftly achieves accomplishment and attains immeasurable, vast merit.
This dharma is profoundly deep and must be held with the utmost reverence.
Among all the methods of the garuḍas,
this dharma is the king and is the most supreme.
If one wishes to subdue all *puttalikas* (dolls/spirits), [this is the means].
If one uses deer meat to kindle the fire,
it will cause people to hate one another. If one desires to cause mutual hatred among people,
one should use the wing feathers of a *huhu* bird to kindle the fire.
If one wishes to subdue a stubborn child,
take the feathers of a pheasant and burn them in fire.
If one wishes to summon a person from afar, [perform the same].
It is accomplished by burning ox-hide meat.
If one recites this one thousand and eight times at each of the three periods of the day, success will be attained.
